title: 카페 · 커피
intro: '카페'는 자주 가는 카페 묘사 → 카페에 가는 이유와 하는 일 → 기억에 남는 경험 → 예전과 지금의 카페 이용 비교 순서로 출제됩니다. 페르소나는 분당에서 가족과 함께 사는 20년차 개발팀 리드로, 주말 아침마다 아파트에서 걸어서 5분 거리인 중앙공원 옆 작은 카페에서 아메리카노를 마시며 한 시간 동안 책을 읽습니다. '중앙공원 옆 카페, 창가 자리, 혼자만의 시간' 설정 하나로 네 문제를 모두 연결하세요.
strategy: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장(Oh, cafes? Sure, I'd love to talk about my favorite cafe.) → 기본 정보(어디·얼마나 가까운지) → 세부(내부 모습·하는 일) → 느낌·이유(바쁜 한 주 뒤의 혼자만의 시간) → 마무리 문장(Yeah, that's my favorite cafe.)
카페는 '중앙공원 옆, 집에서 걸어서 5분, 작지만 아늑한 곳' 하나로 고정하세요. 커피 냄새, 나무 테이블, 식물, 큰 창문 정도면 묘사가 충분합니다.
루틴은 토요일 아침 8시 가족이 자는 동안 집을 나섬 → 아메리카노 주문 → 창가 자리에서 휴대폰 무음, 책 읽기 → 한 시간 뒤 아이들 줄 빵 사서 귀가 순서로 말하세요.
경험은 '비 오는 토요일, 딸과 함께 간 날 딸이 냅킨에 그린 카페 그림을 사장님이 벽에 붙여 줌', 비교는 '20년 전 신입 땐 친구 만나는 곳·사무실 믹스커피 → 지금은 혼자 쉬는 곳·앱 주문'으로 준비하세요.

expressions.en: Oh, cafes? Sure, I'd love to talk about my favorite cafe.
expressions.ko: 아, 카페요? 네, 제가 제일 좋아하는 카페에 대해 기꺼이 얘기할게요.
expressions.note: 주제 시작 문장: 질문 키워드를 되묻고 시작

expressions.en: There's a small cafe near my apartment.
expressions.ko: 우리 아파트 근처에 작은 카페가 있어요.
expressions.note: There's + 명사 + 장소: 무엇이 어디에 있는지 소개

expressions.en: It's only a five-minute walk from my house.
It's not very big, but it's really cozy.
expressions.note: not very ~, but ~: 단점 뒤에 장점 붙이기

expressions.en: I usually order a hot Americano.
expressions.note: order: 주문하다 / iced Americano: 아이스 아메리카노

expressions.en: I go there on weekend mornings to read a book.
expressions.ko: 주말 아침마다 책을 읽으러 거기 가요.

expressions.en: I sometimes buy some pastries for my kids.
expressions.note: buy A for B: B에게 주려고 A를 사다

expressions.en: When you walk in, the first thing you notice is the smell of coffee.
expressions.ko: 들어가면 제일 먼저 커피 향이 느껴져요.

expressions.en: It has a warm atmosphere that makes me feel relaxed.
I put my phone on silent so nobody can bother me.
expressions.ko: 아무도 방해하지 못하게 휴대폰을 무음으로 해 둬요.
expressions.note: put ~ on silent: 무음으로 하다 / so (that) + 주어 + can: ~하도록

expressions.en: These days, people tend to use cafes like offices.
expressions.ko: 요즘 사람들은 카페를 사무실처럼 쓰는 경향이 있어요.

expressions.en: I order ahead with an app, which saves a lot of time.
expressions.ko: 앱으로 미리 주문하는데, 그게 시간을 많이 아껴 줘요.
expressions.note: , which: 앞 문장 전체를 받는 관계대명사

expressions.en: It feels like my little hideaway from a busy week.
expressions.ko: 바쁜 한 주에서 벗어나는 저만의 작은 은신처 같아요.

expressions.en: I quietly slip out of the apartment while my family is still asleep.
expressions.ko: 가족이 아직 자는 동안 조용히 집을 빠져나와요.
네, 그게 제가 제일 좋아하는 카페예요.

questions.en: You indicated in the survey that you like going to cafes. Tell me about a cafe you often go to. Where is it, and what does it look like?
questions.ko: 설문에서 카페 가는 걸 좋아한다고 하셨네요. 자주 가는 카페에 대해 말해 주세요. 어디에 있고, 어떻게 생겼나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 위치(중앙공원 옆, 집에서 걸어서 5분) → 내부 묘사(나무 테이블, 식물, 큰 창) → 좋은 이유(조용하고 아늑함) → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
들어가서 보이는 순서대로(입구 → 카운터 → 자리 → 창밖) 묘사하면 길을 잃지 않아요
냄새(smell of coffee)나 음악(soft jazz) 같은 감각 묘사 한 문장이 점수를 올려 줘요

answers.IM3: Oh, cafes? Sure, I'd love to talk about my favorite cafe. There's a small cafe near my apartment in Bundang. It's only a five-minute walk from my house, right next to Central Park. It's not very big, but it's really cozy. There are wooden tables and lots of plants inside. Big windows face the park, so it's bright in the morning. I usually go there on weekend mornings to read a book. Yeah, that's my favorite cafe.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about the cafe I often go to. I'm the kind of person who loves a quiet cup of coffee on weekend mornings, so I have a favorite spot. It's a small cafe near Central Park, and it's only a five-minute walk from my house. When you walk in, the first thing you notice is the smell of fresh coffee. The owner roasts the beans right there. There are about eight wooden tables, a long counter, and lots of green plants. My favorite seat is by the big window, because I can see people walking in the park. They play soft jazz, and it's never too crowded in the morning. It has a warm atmosphere that makes me feel relaxed. So yeah, that's the cafe I go to almost every weekend.
answers.AL: Oh, cafes? Let me think. Well, there are tons of cafes in my neighborhood, but there's one little place I keep going back to. It's tucked away on a quiet street right next to Central Park, and it's only a five-minute walk from my apartment, which is perfect for me. From the outside, it doesn't look like much, just a small brick building with a wooden sign. But when you walk in, the first thing you notice is the rich smell of coffee, because the owner roasts the beans in the back. Inside, it's not very big, maybe eight or nine tables, but every corner feels cozy. There are wooden tables, shelves full of old books, and plants hanging from the ceiling. My favorite seat is a corner table by the big window, where the morning sun comes in and I can watch people jogging and walking their dogs in the park. The owner is a friendly guy around my age, and he already knows my order, a hot Americano with no sugar. There's soft jazz playing in the background, so it's the perfect place to sit with a book for an hour. Honestly, it feels like my little hideaway from a busy week. So yeah, that's pretty much my favorite cafe.

questions.en: Why do you go to cafes, and what do you usually do there? Tell me about what you typically do from the moment you arrive until you leave.
questions.ko: 왜 카페에 가고, 거기서 주로 무엇을 하나요? 도착해서 나올 때까지 보통 하는 일을 말해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 왜 가는지(혼자만의 조용한 시간) → 언제·누구와(토요일 아침, 혼자) → 도착부터 나올 때까지(주문 → 창가 자리 → 독서 → 빵 사서 귀가) → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
First, Then, Before I leave 로 순서를 잡으면 루틴이 깔끔해져요
이유는 '평일엔 회의와 메시지, 집에선 아이들'처럼 대비로 말하면 설득력이 생겨요

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about what I do at cafes. I usually go to a cafe on Saturday or Sunday morning. I go there alone because I want some quiet time. First, I order a hot Americano. Then, I sit by the window and read a book. I usually stay for about an hour. Before I leave, I sometimes buy some muffins for my kids. Yeah, that's what I usually do at cafes.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about why I go to cafes. I mostly go to a cafe for some quiet time on weekend mornings. My weekdays are full of meetings and messages, and at home, my kids are always busy and noisy. So I go to the cafe near Central Park around eight on Saturday morning. I usually go alone because my family likes to sleep in. First, I order an Americano. Then, I find a seat by the window and open my book. These days, I'm reading some history books and novels. I put my phone on silent so nobody can bother me. I usually stay about an hour. Before I leave, I buy some pastries for my family, so everyone is happy when I get home. It helps me recharge before a busy week. So yeah, that's pretty much my cafe routine.
answers.AL: Oh, why I go to cafes? Let me think. Well, for me, a cafe isn't really about the coffee. It's about having an hour to myself. During the week, I'm in meetings all day, my phone keeps buzzing with messages from my team, and at home, there's always something going on with the kids. So on Saturday mornings, I quietly slip out of the apartment while my family is still asleep and walk to my favorite cafe near Central Park. The owner usually starts making my Americano the moment he sees me at the door, which always makes me smile. First, I grab my coffee and settle into the corner seat by the window. Then, I put my phone on silent and open whatever book I'm reading. Lately it's been a mystery novel that I just can't put down. Every once in a while, I look up and watch people jogging in the park. After about an hour, I order a few croissants and muffins to go, because if I come home empty-handed, my kids definitely let me know about it. Honestly, that hour helps me recharge more than anything else. Yeah, that's my little cafe ritual.

questions.en: Tell me about a memorable experience you had at a cafe. What happened, who were you with, and why was it so memorable?
questions.ko: 카페에서 있었던 기억에 남는 경험을 말해 주세요. 무슨 일이 있었고, 누구와 함께였으며, 왜 그렇게 기억에 남나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 언제·누구와(비 오는 토요일, 초등학생 딸) → 무슨 일(함께 책 읽기, 딸이 냅킨에 그린 그림) → 반전(사장님이 벽에 붙여 줌) → 느낌 → 'So yeah, that's ~' 마무리
과거 시제로 일관되게, To my surprise 로 반전 포인트를 표시하세요
마지막에 '그 그림이 아직도 걸려 있다'처럼 현재와 연결하면 여운이 남아요

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about a memorable time at a cafe. I remember one time when my daughter came with me on a rainy Saturday. She ordered a hot chocolate, and I had my Americano. We sat by the window and read our books together. Then she drew a picture of the cafe on a napkin. The owner liked it a lot, and he put it on the wall. She was so proud. Yeah, that's my most memorable cafe experience.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about a memorable cafe experience. I remember one time when my daughter came with me on a rainy Saturday. Usually I go to the cafe alone, but that day she woke up early and asked to come. She's in elementary school, so she was really excited. She ordered a hot chocolate with whipped cream, and I got my usual Americano. We sat by the window, and I read my book while she read a comic book. After a while, she started drawing the cafe on a napkin, with the plants and the rain outside. When we were leaving, she showed it to the owner. To my surprise, the owner put her drawing up on the wall next to the counter. She was so proud, and she still talks about it. So yeah, that's a day I'll always remember.
answers.AL: Oh, a memorable cafe experience? Let me think. Well, one rainy Saturday morning really stands out. Normally, my cafe time is my alone time, but that day my daughter, who's in elementary school, woke up early and begged to come with me. I wasn't sure at first, because I thought she'd get bored in five minutes, but I said okay. We shared an umbrella on the walk over, and she chatted the whole way. answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you how I use cafes now. Twenty years ago, I used to go to cafes to meet friends, but now I go there to have some quiet time. Back then, there weren't many cafes, and coffee was pretty expensive. At work, we just drank instant coffee. Now there are cafes everywhere in my neighborhood. I usually go alone on weekend mornings and read a book for an hour. Yeah, that's how my cafe life has changed.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about how I use cafes differently now. When I was a new employee about twenty years ago, there weren't as many cafes as there are now. Coffee from a cafe was kind of a treat, and at the office, we mostly drank instant coffee mix from paper cups. I used to go to cafes to meet friends, but now I go there to have some quiet time. Back then, cafes were loud places to chat for hours. These days, people tend to use cafes like offices. You see lots of people working on laptops or studying. Also, I order ahead with an app now, which saves a lot of time. The biggest difference for me is the reason I go. Now a cafe is my place to rest and read. So yeah, that's how my cafe habits have changed.
answers.AL: Oh, that's an interesting question. Let me think. Well, my cafe habits have changed a lot over the past twenty years. When I first started working, cafes weren't on every corner like they are now. A cup of coffee from a cafe felt a bit fancy, so at the office, we mostly drank instant coffee mix from paper cups, sometimes four or five a day. Back then, I used to go to cafes on weekends to meet my college friends in Seoul, and we'd sit there for hours, talking and laughing loudly. Now it's pretty much the opposite. I go alone on weekend mornings, and the whole point is to be quiet and read. Cafes themselves have changed, too. These days, people tend to treat them like offices or study rooms, so you see rows of people with laptops and headphones. Ordering is different as well. I just tap my phone, and my coffee is ready when I walk in. I think this change is because of how busy everyone has become. People need a place that's not home and not work, and for me, a cafe is exactly that. So yeah, that's how cafes went from a place to hang out to my personal escape.
